questions.stem: 提示：有些學校會帶都市的學生到鄉下參加插秧體驗，讓他們親自下田，認識每天吃的米從哪裡來。請比較下列兩張圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一與圖二兩種認識稻米的方式有何不同；第二段說明你認為學校是否值得安排這類下田體驗，並提出理由支持你的看法。

1.explanation_zh: 第一段是「比較」，兩張圖都要寫，而且要寫出差異，不是各自描述完就結束；第二段要先表態，再提出理由。贊成或反對都可以，重點是理由要具體，例如自己或同學下田的經驗、對食物態度的改變。
evidence: 第一段比較圖一與圖二兩種認識稻米的方式有何不同
並提出理由支持你的看法
1.strategy_zh: 比較段可以抓三組對比：地點（教室／田裡）、身體（坐著／彎腰）、反應（無聊／投入）。
hints: 第一段：每組對比都用轉折或對照的轉承語連起來
第二段：立場一句，理由用列舉轉承分開寫
加一句讓步（例如費用或安全）再拉回立場，說服力更強

moves.zh: 比較圖一與圖二兩種認識稻米的方式有何不同

提出理由支持你的看法

content.focus_zh: 第一段要寫出兩種方式的對比（坐著看 vs. 動手做、舒適但無聊 vs. 辛苦但投入）；第二段要有明確立場（值得或不值得），至少兩個理由，理由最好有親身經驗或具體細節，而不是只說「很有意義」。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段以「圖一…；相較之下，圖二…」對照；第二段先表態，再以列舉轉承逐一提出理由，可加一句讓步（費用、安全）再回到立場。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。

看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在式或現在進行式，經驗用過去式；比較級（learn more from doing than from watching）與讓步句（Although …）要寫對。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 農事相關的字（plant、rice field、mud、farmer、bend over）要拼對，避免整段只用 interesting、meaningful。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

圖二：捲起褲管在泥田裡插秧，有人皺眉、有人大笑

outline.topic_sentence_zh: 表明學校是否值得安排下田體驗。
details_zh: 理由一：動手做比看影片學得多（可用自己的經驗）
理由二：學會珍惜食物、了解農夫的辛苦
讓步：費用與安全，但可以克服

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show two different ways for students to learn about rice. In the first picture, a class is sitting in an air-conditioned classroom and watching a video of rice fields. Some students are yawning, and one boy is even sleeping on his desk. In the second picture, by contrast, students have rolled up their pants and are standing in a muddy field without shoes. They are bending over and putting young rice plants into the mud while a farmer shows them how to do it. Although some of them look uncomfortable, most of them are laughing.
I think schools should arrange this kind of farm trip for students. First of all, students can learn more from doing than from watching. For example, last spring my class spent a day planting rice in Yilan. My back hurt after only twenty minutes, so I finally understood why farming is such hard work. Second, the experience teaches students to respect food. Since that trip, I have never left any rice in my lunch box. Of course, a trip like this takes time and money, but the lessons it teaches cannot be learned from a screen. In short, a day in the fields is worth more than many hours in a classroom.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
Learning where rice comes from can happen in two very different settings. In the first picture, about thirty students sit in a cool classroom, facing a screen that shows green rice fields and a farmer working in the distance. The scene is comfortable but lifeless: a few students are yawning, one has fallen asleep on his desk, and only two in the front row are taking notes. The second picture, in contrast, is full of movement. With their pants rolled up to their knees, a dozen students are wading through a flooded field and pushing bundles of rice seedlings into the mud, while a farmer in a straw hat demonstrates how far apart the plants should be. Some of them frown as their feet sink into the cold mud; others burst out laughing at their friends’ muddy legs. One setting delivers information, whereas the other turns it into a memory.
In my opinion, schools should definitely make room for such trips, even if they cost a day of regular classes. The most obvious reason is that physical experience leaves a more profound impression than any video. For example, when my class visited a farm in Hualien last spring, I expected a relaxing outing. Instead, after twenty minutes of bending over in the mud, my back ached, and I had planted only two crooked rows. As a result, that tedious, painful afternoon taught me more about the value of a bowl of rice than any textbook had. Another reason is that these trips connect city teenagers with people they rarely meet. The farmer who guided us explained that a single field needs months of care and that one typhoon can destroy everything overnight. Hearing this from him, rather than reading it online, made me realize how vulnerable a harvest is. Admittedly, such trips require transportation, insurance, and careful planning, and some parents may worry about safety. However, these obstacles can be overcome, whereas a generation that sees food only as a product on a shelf may grow up wasting it without a second thought. All in all, a single day in the mud is a small investment in students’ respect for food and for the people who grow it.

steady.comment_zh: 第一段以 by contrast 對照冷氣教室打呵欠、趴睡與光腳下田插秧、農夫示範；第二段先表態，兩個理由（做中學、學會惜食）各配一個宜蘭插秧的具體經驗，並有一句讓步（時間與金錢）。比較級 learn more from doing than from watching、Although 讓步句、現在完成式都正確，無語言錯誤；篇幅精簡，字彙平實。most of them are laughing 略誇大（圖中是有的皺眉、有的笑）。

top.comment_zh: 第一段 comfortable but lifeless 與 full of movement 的對照鮮明，細節（斗笠農夫示範間距、腳陷泥中、笑對方的泥腿）完整，收在 delivers information vs. turns it into a memory；第二段兩個理由（身體經驗、認識農人）都有具體經驗，讓步交通、保險、安全後再回到立場。句型與字彙（wading、seedlings、vulnerable、profound）都在高水準，無語言錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段用 by contrast 對照坐在冷氣教室看影片（打呵欠、睡覺）與光腳插秧（彎腰、農夫示範、有人笑）；第二段立場明確，有兩個理由（做中學、學會珍惜食物）、宜蘭插秧的經驗與讓步（花時間、花錢）。文法、拼字都正確；用字貼切（air-conditioned、bending over），句型以簡單句與連接詞為主。

top.comment_zh: 第一段把兩張圖寫成「資訊」與「記憶」的對比，細節完整；第二段有兩個理由（身體經驗、與農夫接觸）、花蓮插秧的經驗、農夫的話，並讓步（交通、保險、安全）後回到立場。句型與字彙豐富，文法、拼字無誤。

issues_zh: 圖一只畫了 12 個學生，但圖說與 E2 寫「約三十名」（about thirty）；圖二只畫了 4 名學生，圖說與 E2 寫「十幾名」（a dozen）。考生看圖會數到比較少的人數。建議圖說與範文改成與圖一致的描述，或把圖補足。
